codeReview.summary: The worker added 4 well-structured edge-case tests to tests/unit/test_e2e_pipeline_integration.py covering all four scenarios specified in the feature description: (1) all-stages-failing, (2) forensics-disabled configuration, (3) invalid binary path, and (4) recompilation stage graceful failure. Two reusable helper functions (_make_stage_result and _make_pipeline_result) were added to reduce boilerplate. All 6 tests (2 original + 4 new) pass. The implementation cleanly exercises the EndToEndPipelineRunner class through monkeypatched execute_pipeline calls, verifying both return value structure and state side-effects (e.g., pipeline execution JSON written to disk). The code style is consistent with the existing test file conventions, uses proper type hints, and passes flake8 lint.

issues.description: test_runner_marks_all_stages_failing_as_failed: The stage results passed to _make_pipeline_result all use the default StageStatus.COMPLETED status, but the test is asserting 'failed' behavior. The test works because the unified_report output dict controls the reported status, not the StageResult statuses. This is technically correct given how EndToEndPipelineRunner.run() derives status from report_output.get('status'), but it means the test doesn't fully exercise the failure path at the pipeline engine level — it relies on the mock pre-writing a failed report to disk. Acceptable for a unit test but worth noting.

test_runner_resolves_invalid_binary_path_before_execution: The test verifies that the runner resolves the path and returns a failed result dict, but it doesn't verify that the runner itself raises or logs any warning about the missing file. The runner delegates binary existence checking to the pipeline engine, so this is an integration concern, not a unit test gap. Acceptable.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The new tests use Python 3.10+ type union syntax (dict | None, list[StageResult]) in function signatures. The AGENTS.md coding conventions state Python 3.9+ compatibility. These type hints appear in function signatures of helper functions used only at test time with 'from __future__ import annotations', which makes them strings and avoids runtime errors on 3.9. This is fine but could be confusing for future contributors who copy the pattern without the future import.
